text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us real-world data on how it behaves across different contributor types, repos, and edge cases—no guesswork. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR comments, but that’s minor compared to missing hidden issues. After the week, we’ll have hard evidence to decide if we expand to new contributors only or roll it out fully.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode risks normalizing PR-Agent noise—reviewers will ignore *all* comments, including real ones, once the experiment ends. A better alternative: run it on a single repo first, measure comment-to-action ratios, then expand only if the signal-to-noise ratio justifies the cost. Settle it with a week of data showing at least 30% of PR-Agent comments trigger meaningful changes.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* PRs from new contributors for two weeks to limit noise while still catching edge cases. If the comment-to-action ratio exceeds 3:1, expand to all PRs—otherwise, drop the experiment.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* new-contributor PRs for two weeks. This keeps noise low while still catching edge cases early—new contributors are likelier to miss subtle issues that PR-Agent flags. The trade-off is missing problems in experienced-contributor PRs, but those are already lower-risk. If the comment-to-action ratio hits 3:1, expand to all PRs; otherwise, drop it.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* new-contributor PRs for two weeks, measuring comment-to-action ratios to decide next steps.

Result: Noise stays low while we catch early issues. Owner: Overhaul.
